tagline: Latin America's leading beverage company with diversified portfolio in beer, wine, and non-alcoholic drinks
hero_kpi_rationale: EBITDA margin is CCU's key KPI, reflecting operational profitability and the company's ability to manage costs and pricing amid a challenging macroeconomic environment (currency devaluations, inflation in Argentina, commodity volatility). It demonstrates the group's operational resilience.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after deducting direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin improved by 55 basis points as a percentage of sales, driven by the appreciation of the Chilean peso against the dollar and efficiency gains, despite rising aluminum costs.
kpis.signal: Gross margin improved slightly despite cost pressures from aluminum and currency headwinds

kpis.name: EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a measure of core profitability.
kpis.description: EBITDA remained nearly stable, supported by strong performance in Chile (+13.7%), offsetting declines in International America (-18.6%) and Wine (-50.1%).
kpis.signal: EBITDA remained stable despite strong Chilean performance offsetting international headwinds

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by the company.
kpis.description: Sales growth was nearly flat (+0.2%) despite a 1.8% increase in volumes, due to a 1.5% decline in average prices in Chilean pesos, impacted by ARS depreciation against the USD.
kpis.signal: Revenue growth modest due to pricing pressure offset by volume gains in Chile

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Final profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income declined by 6.8% to 53.9 billion CLP, primarily due to margin contraction in the international and wine segments.
kpis.signal: Net income declined despite operational stability due to international segment and wine margin compression

kpis.name: Consolidated Volumes
kpis.explanation: Total quantity of products sold by the company in billions of units.
kpis.description: Consolidated volumes increased by 1.8%, driven by a 3.9% expansion in Chile, despite declines in International America (-1.7%) and Wine (-5.9%).
kpis.signal: Volume growth driven by strong Chilean performance offsetting international weakness

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: EBITDA expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: EBITDA margin remained unchanged at 16.1%, reflecting balanced management of growth, costs, and pricing amid commodity volatility and exchange rate fluctuations.
kpis.signal: EBITDA margin resilient at 16.1% despite commodity volatility and currency headwinds

risks.title: Dependence on brand licensing agreements
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified in A.1 with moderate language ('could negatively impact'). CCU operates under licensing agreements with specific conditions; however, 70% of sales come from owned brands by 2025, mitigating impact. Trend stable. Category weight medium for beverage sector.

risks.title: Volatility in raw material and input costs
risks.score_rationale: Risk detailed in A.2 with strong language ('exposed to market volatility', 'variables which the Company has no control over'). Multiple factors: exchange rates, climate, geopolitics. Linked to PUSU (15% recycled plastic obligation 2025-2030). Trend up (inflationary pressure 2022-2025). Category weight very high for beverage producer.

risks.title: Shortage of raw materials and critical inputs
risks.score_rationale: Autonomous risk in A.3 with direct language ('eventual shortage', 'could affect the Company's supply chain'). Multiple causes: consumption shifts, agricultural production, quality/availability, logistics. Explicit link to PUSU. Trend up (post-COVID supply chain tensions). Category weight critical for production.

risks.title: Geographic concentration: reliance on Chile and Argentina
risks.score_rationale: Major risk in A.4 with detailed exposure: Chile 64% of revenue, Argentina 27% (International segment). Strong language on macroeconomic volatility, inflation (12.8% in 2022), currency controls (2019-2023), price controls (2020-2023). Argentina has been hyperinflationary since 2018. Trend stable but fragile context. Category weight very high.

risks.title: Antitrust risks and abuse of dominant position
risks.score_rationale: Risk detailed in B.1 with concrete cases: ongoing litigation in Chile for abuse of dominant position in on-premise beer market; FNE commitment on anti-competitive practices (microbreweries). Moderate language but explicit financial/reputational risks. Trend stable. Category weight high for market leader.

risks.title: Regulatory changes in labeling and advertising
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in B.3 with concrete example: Chilean Law 21,363 (alcohol advertising restrictions, warnings, time/event limitations). Moderate language ('constantly changing', 'could impact'). Trend up (increasing health/wellness regulation). Category weight medium for alcohol/beverage sector.

risks.title: Changing lifestyles and consumer preferences
risks.score_rationale: Structural risk in A.6 with nuanced language ('some structural, others transitory'). Causes: COVID-19, digital entertainment, individualism, public safety, health/wellness trends. CCU acknowledges innovation capacity but risk of disruption. Trend up (acceleration post-COVID). Category weight high for beverages.

risks.title: Retention of critical talent and operational continuity
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified in A.5 with moderate language ('could negatively affect'). Impacts: operational continuity, strategic execution, innovation, loss of knowledge. No specific turnover data. Trend stable. Category weight medium for manufacturing sector.
